newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Kuchma names industrialist 1st deputy PM.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Kuchma names industrialist 1st deputy PM.

text.p: President Leonid Kuchma on Friday named Anatoly Holubchenko, an industrialist, first deputy prime minister of Ukraine, a spokesman for Kuchma's office said.
Holubchenko, 47, is a member of the pro-Kuchma Constitutional Centre in parliament and was industry minister from 1992 to 1995.
It was the latest appointment to the former Soviet republic's new cabinet after a reshuffle which began last month following the resignation of prime minister Pavlo Lazarenko.
A metallurgist by trade, Holubchenko was deputy head of a big steelworks and a member of the state metals committee.
His appointment could signal support for troubled heavy industry which has struggled since independence in 1991 and Kuchma's wish to back producers in the country of 51 million.

Kuchma's spokesman said the reshuffle, which followed an almost six-month delay in approving the 1997 budget and a postponement of a big International Monetary Fund loan, was aimed at speeding up economic reforms.
